cohort: The study involved 374 pregnant women, equally divided into hypertensive (n=187) and normotensive (n=187) groups.
finding: Women with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy had significantly increased risks of preterm birth, stillbirth, low birth weight, early neonatal death, perinatal death, and cesarean section delivery compared to normotensive women.
mod_finding: Women with hypertensive disorders had a 1.7 times higher risk of cesarean section delivery compared with normotensive women.
followup_time: Up to early neonatal period (first 7 days post-birth) for perinatal outcomes
